q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance $g active) predicates the property of the group symbol, the form Categorical statements and Quantifiers explicitly bar ("never a bare (Inheritance <group> <prop>) on the group symbol"); a faithful statement sends a copular predicate on a plural through the per-member distribution rule, so this conjunct can bind nothing.

q2_gaps: a counting question over a COPULAR predicate ("how many X are ADJ?") — Counting questions gives only the verbal "How many X V?" shape, where the group is bound through an event; there is no licensed conjunct that reads a member property off a group

counting the individuals that satisfy a predicate when no group witness carrying a Cardinality was ever minted — only FoldAll over stored group cardinalities is provided, and it is reserved for explicit aggregate-total questions
review.notes: GroupOf/Cardinality binding and the lowercase kind lemma keeper (a capitalized plural quantified over, not referring as a name) are right; the single non-union line is correct for an unbounded how-many question.

issues.reason: Partitives states the one deliberate exception — a property of a subset group takes Inheritance, not Member — so (GroupOf $g keeper) (Cardinality $g $n) (Inheritance $g active) is exactly the storage a cardinal partitive ("three of the Keepers are active") lays down and the conjunct does bind; the quoted bar governs asserting a universal over a definite group, and the residual miss against the per-member distribution rule is the coverage gap the reviewer itself files, not a parse defect.

gaps_confirmed: a counting question over a COPULAR predicate ("how many X are ADJ?") — Counting questions gives only the verbal shape, where the group binds through an event; a plural's copular predicate is stored as a per-member distribution rule, which exposes no conjunct a query can read off the group

counting the individuals that satisfy a predicate when no group witness carrying a Cardinality was ever minted — only FoldAll over stored group cardinalities is provided, and it is reserved for explicit aggregate-total questions
new_gaps: a plain "how many X …?" has no dual-storage union partner: Counting questions unions Cardinality with CardinalityAtLeast / CardinalityAtMost only for a BOUNDED question, so a group whose size is stored as a bound or as a CardinalityPhrase ("several Keepers are active") is unreachable by the how-many query as the instruction set writes it
adjudication.notes: The single line binds the partitive storage and nothing else, but with no licensed conjunct for the per-member rule that is the most the instruction set allows here. The lowercase kind lemma keeper is right for a capitalized plural being quantified over rather than referring as a name.
